correctness.rationale: For finite commutative chain rings R, the UT3 commutator equals the determinant ab′-a′b. Valuation s and primitive projective directions over R/(pi^(ell-s)) give determinant-zero adjacency; uniform q-to-one lifts give the same rooted direction forest for all rings of residue size q and length ell. Centralizer size q^(2ell+s) yields exactly ell noncentral degrees and recovers (q,ell) from the graph. Thus the full graph is a function exactly of (q,ell). Explicit R=Z/8 and S=F2[t]/(t^3) have the same graph and non-isomorphic abelian central quotients C8^2 vs C2^6 and derived groups C8 vs C2^3, so cannot be isoclinic. The projective primitive-pair lemma and determinant valuation boundary s+t>=ell were reconstructed. Independent exact integer centralizer checks across length 1,2,3 models corroborate but do not replace this infinite-family proof.

evidence: Two-generated result determines graphs/isoclinism within that restricted family; H(F2[t]/t^3) has C2^6 central quotient and is not two-generated.

originality.rationale: The published Arvind--Cameron 2022 class-two isoclinism conjecture, not simply the field construction, is directly negated by a concrete family member. The known two-generated class-two commuting-graph theorem applies to groups with a two-generator quotient and therefore does not cover H(F2[t]/t^3) with a six-generator central quotient. Full-graph rather than noncentral-graph convention and characteristic independence distinguish the statement. Best-of-knowledge PASS with explicit priority risk.

value.rationale: A concrete counterexample to a named group-theoretic conjecture together with an all-length combinatorial classification of full commuting graphs is substantive structural mathematics. Graph degrees recover ring size/length but lose additive exponent, a useful obstruction to graph-based isoclinism recognition.

limitations: Finite commutative chain rings only; full simple commuting graph including center; UT3 only. Not all class-two groups or nonchain local rings.
